title: Why Does Your Mouth Water When You Imagine a LEMON? 🍋
description:
Imagine biting a juicy lemon, and your mouth starts watering, even though there's no lemon. Your brain takes a practice bite: picturing the taste is enough to switch on your spit glands early, under your tongue and inside your cheeks. Lemon means acid, so the spit gets there first, to wash and protect your teeth. In one study, people drooled just watching a video of a man eating a lemon, and the ones who drooled the most tended to care the most about other people. Is your mouth watering? Yes or no?

Subscribe for a new strange question every day.
